target_customer: Residential developers and homebuyers in the Pacific Northwest, plus real estate fund investors (the company is also its own developer and general contractor)
problem: Construction costs are rising and the construction workforce is shrinking while cities face a housing shortage; NODE's flat-pack kits aim to cut build time and labor.
business_model: Hardware kit manufacturing plus vertically integrated development, general contracting and real estate fund management
product_category: Prefab and mass timber residential construction tech

founders.name: Bec Wilder
founders.role: CEO of Green Canopy NODE and co-founder of NODE (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists the name Bec Wilder. A December 2021 company blog post and 2018 to 2021 press name the NODE co-founder as Bec Chapin, likely the same person but not confirmed by sources. YC bio mentions Board Director of the Washington Mass Timber Accelerator.

competitors.name: Blokable
competitors.what: Seattle startup making steel-frame modular homes designed for stacking into multi-family units

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing flat-pack house kits that fit shipping containers and assemble without specialists, plus running a factory, is hard manufacturing and engineering work but not research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Prefab homebuilding was widely attempted; the vertical integration with a developer gave a built-in pipeline but designs and process were replicable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge in the sources found; NODE merged with a local developer, Green Canopy, in November 2021.

market_need_then: Housing shortage in major cities and rising construction costs and labor scarcity, as stated in the company's YC description (2019).

branding.domain_note: NODE used node.eco; the merged company uses greencanopynode.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission and sustainability framing: homes, relationships and businesses that regenerate communities and environments (YC description)

rebrands.why: Merger of the two companies, announced November 2021 and described in a December 2021 company blog

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press (Dwell, GeekWire, Quartz) covered the NODE product, but no source shows a brand-driven community; the NODE name is shared with the Node.js brand, a possible search confusion.

pivots.from: NODE standalone flat-pack house kit maker
pivots.to: Merged with Green Canopy developer and fund manager as Green Canopy NODE
pivots.why: Merger described as vertically integrating the kit maker with a developer, contractor and fund manager

outcome_analysis: NODE entered YC in 2019 as a flat-pack prefab kit maker in Seattle and merged with developer Green Canopy in November 2021, closing a 10 million dollar round. The company is active with about 31 people. The sources do not show revenue or unit economics, so success or stall cannot be judged; the merger suggests a move to vertical integration.
notes: Company website fetch was blocked by a safety-check rate limit and GeekWire returned 403; the competitor entry rests on a search result summary of the 2018 GeekWire article. Seedtable lists the 2021 round as seed with Techstars Ventures and others; CB Insights reports 8.95M total and PitchBook 31.1M, so totals are unverified and the stage is recorded as other. A 2023 StartEngine equity crowdfunding raise exists but its amount was not verified. Education and prior employers not found. No outcome news beyond the merger.
